transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Well, my family keeps saying I’m doing too much. But somebody has to get this move handled, rebuild the new garage properly, keep things organized at church, and show the younger guys at work how the job ought to be done. I just feel like I’m the one with the drive to do it.
Over the past week or so, have you noticed you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to my sleep, honestly.
Would you say this level of drive and need to control every project is new for you over the past couple of weeks, or is this basically how you've always been for as long as you can remember?
No, this isn’t how I’ve always been. It’s been about a month now, since we were forced to start leaving the old house.
Has this drive and need to control everything caused serious problems—like conflicts at work, financial risks, or family relationships—that others have had to step in about?

Yeah. I got pulled from work after a safety incident. And at home, my wife and the family have stopped trusting me to make decisions about money, driving, or the move. They say things got out of hand.

Before this past month, have you ever had earlier periods—lasting days or weeks—where your mood, energy, or activity level was noticeably different from your usual self, either unusually high or unusually low?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of any earlier stretches like that before this past month.
Have you ever gone through a period lasting two weeks or more where you felt unusually sad, hopeless, or lost interest in almost everything?
I don’t think so. I can’t recall a time where I felt that way for two weeks straight.
